title: About the project
standfirst: TRIAD co-creates and tests a framework that balances foundational competences, transversal competences and AI literacy in secondary schools and vocational education, with learner well-being built in.
context:
Across Europe, adolescents are growing up in a digital environment shaped by generative AI, smartphones and social media. These technologies transform how they learn, communicate and prepare for future careers. The tools enable creativity, personalisation and collaboration, but evidence on their impact on learning and well-being is fragmented and often lags behind practice.

TRIAD addresses this gap by co-creating and testing an integrated framework that balances foundational competences (literacy, numeracy, science), transversal competences (critical thinking, collaboration, metacognition) and AI and digital literacies, while embedding safeguards for cognitive, emotional and social well-being.

The project focuses on learners aged 12 to 18 in secondary schools and vocational education and training (VET), where competences must be consolidated and inequality risks peak.

challenges.title: Skills and depth of learning
challenges.text: TRIAD studies whether relying on AI weakens skills and makes learning shallower, and under which conditions it does the opposite.

challenges.title: Competence frameworks
challenges.text: TRIAD studies how foundational, transversal and AI competences can be brought into one framework with clear pathways, where today's frameworks stand apart.

challenges.title: Readiness and equity
challenges.text: TRIAD studies how ready schools and learners are, and whether AI in the classroom widens or narrows socio-economic and digital divides.

challenges.title: Well-being
challenges.text: TRIAD studies how learning with digital and AI tools relates to adolescents' well-being, where the evidence so far points in different directions.

approach: Through large-scale classroom pilots across Europe, combined with neuroscientific methods (EEG and fNIRS), TRIAD studies when AI genuinely enhances learning rather than replacing it. Classroom scenarios are validated across diverse contexts and enriched by input from SMEs and labour market actors.
results: The project works towards classroom-ready designs, developmental pathways for students and teachers, and policy recommendations, to help schools adopt AI responsibly. This is in line with the European Education Area 2030 and the Digital Education Action Plan.
workplan_note: Month 1 is September 2026. Work package titles, leads and months are those of the Grant Agreement.

path.title: Review and framework
path.text: A review of pedagogical models, competence frameworks and AI-supported tools.

path.title: Co-creation
path.text: Pedagogical patterns and classroom scenarios designed with teachers, school leaders, students and VET trainers.

path.title: Pre-test pilots
path.text: Two to three scenarios per country in Croatia, Germany and Greece, with about 300 to 360 learners.

path.title: EU-wide pilots
path.text: Pre-test and post-test with control groups in Lithuania, Germany, Croatia, Finland, Italy and Greece, with about 1,000 learners.

path.title: Analysis and adoption
path.text: Analysis across countries, then toolkits, training modules and policy recommendations.

connect_text: The work is organised in four phases. Each one feeds the TRIAD competence framework or draws on it. A participation strategy and data management and ethics run around all of them.
